nom: Kiehl's Since 1851 Rare Earth Pore-Minimizing Clay Mask

segments.oily: Reviewers with oily or acne-prone oily skin, including combination-oily skin and one reviewer's oily-skinned husband, say the mask draws out excess oil and shine without over-drying, and several consider it best suited to oilier skin types.
segments.dry: Dry-skin reviewers are split: a few say the mask is too drying and left visible dry patches, but a larger group — including several who say they normally avoid clay masks — report the current formulation doesn't strip their dry skin as long as they follow up with a moisturizer.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers, including combination-oily and combination-sensitive skin, say the mask works well, particularly when applied only to the T-zone or oilier areas.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers, including several with rosacea, mostly report the reformulated mask doesn't burn, sting or leave redness the way other clay masks did for them, though one reviewer with sensitive skin still experienced tingling, burning and some redness.
segments.mature: The one reviewer who identifies as having mature, postmenopausal skin says the mask did not feel overly drying despite her skin type.

concerns.dehydration: Reviewers who mention dryness or tightness are split: several say the mask leaves visible dry patches or a 'crazy dry' feeling that requires double moisturizing afterward, especially in cold or winter conditions, while others say the current formulation leaves skin soft rather than stripped, provided they moisturize right after.
concerns.redness: Most reviewers who mention redness or rosacea say the mask calms existing redness or, unlike other clay masks they've tried, doesn't trigger new redness or irritate rosacea; a couple of reviewers still report some redness or a burning sensation immediately after use.
concerns.barrier: A couple of reviewers specifically credit the reformulated, non-stripping version with not disrupting the skin barrier even with regular use, in contrast to how they describe older clay masks behaving.
concerns.blemishes: Acne-prone reviewers generally say the mask dries out active blemishes and clogged pores without over-irritating, including one using it as a spot treatment during pregnancy-safe hormonal breakouts; two reviewers note it can bring underlying pimples to the surface right after use, causing a brief purge that clears up within a day.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily or oily-combination skin consistently say the mask draws out excess oil and reduces shine, particularly when focused on the T-zone, and several consider it best suited to oilier skin types specifically.

aspects.libelle: Tingling or burning for some users
Rinses off easily with no residue
Jar packaging means scooping with fingers
A little goes a long way for the price

extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Wanted to love this, but it made my face feel like it was burning! Unsure what ingredient caused a burning sensation, but it went away after a few minutes. Once I wiped it off, I felt it start burning again.

extraits.titre: Too drying for me, better for oily skin
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] This product did not work for me. It caused dry patches on the areas where I used it. This may be due to my skin being much more dry than usual due to the extremely cold dry weather we are experiencing at the moment. I will definitely try it in the spring and summer when it has a better chance of working for me. It was very smooth to put on. A little goes a long way so this jar would last you forever. If you already have more oily skin as a baseline this may work better for you off the bat than it did for me.

extraits.titre: Good product, just not good for me
extraits.texte: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Okay so I have some mixed feelings because I love Kiehl's products and I noticed maybe the tiniest difference in my pores, but I don't think I'm the intended audience for this product. Solely because I have dry skin and this is marketed for normal, oily, and combination skin (but as I was given this product free in exchange for my review I gotta try it). It did feel nice on the skin and maybe helped a little with my redness but my skin felt so crazy dry after using it that I had to double moisturize. Overall I think it's a good product and would be helpful for others, just not the product for me. So if you have dry skin I probably wouldn't get it but I do think it works well enough.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] Age: 44, Primary skin concerns: Dryness, Redness, Texture, Fine Lines, Occasional blackheads and breakouts, Large sebaceous filament openings Using mask to target: Texture on cheeks, sebaceous filament openings, fine lines (elevens, parentheses) Opinion: Scent: None. This is unscented. If scented skincare bothers you, this won't. Apperance: Light gray, appropriate for a clay mask, but because you have to stick your hand in the tub, kind of messy. I should have used a mask brush, and this could be in a tube. Texture: Squishy, soft, that does adhere but is not sticky (I HAAAATE sticky). It was easy to wipe off my hand. Ingredients: Surprisingly basic. Everything at more than 1% (everything above phenoxyethanol) is either moisturizing or clay (and some titanium dioxide for color). I'm REALLY surprised by how simple this formulation actually is because... Effectiveness: It's surprisingly effective. I wouldn't use it every week, but it really does make a noticeable difference in the texture on my nose and cheeks. I'd absolutely use this before special event makeup for a smoother canvas. NOTE: Other products shown in "after" photo: Murad Multi-Vitamin Infusion Oil (Like I said, I'm dry. Can't do tight, clean skin without something.)

extraits.titre: Simple clay mask that actually works
extraits.texte: I have a super acne prone skin, and it tends to get oily and greasy often. I tried this mask out very recently and since then it has become my go to when my skin feels kinda gross or oily. I use it about once or twice a week, put it on, let it sit, and my skin just feels way cleaner and calmer after. It rinses off easily too and doesn't leave any residue behind. Also, it doesn't sting or dry me out at all, which is nice. Pores on my cheek look less noticeable and my skin feels much smoother. Plus, it helps calm the redness around my nose as well. Overall, good value for money, decent packaging and most importantly it just does the job really well!

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] This mask comes in a clean container and is easy to apply after cleansing due to its creamy texture. It's light on my skin with no strong scent. There is a strong tingling/cooling feeling around my nose when I first put it on and while it was drying, and then a refreshing mild cool feeling stays for the rest of the 10 minutes. It dried very quickly, so it doesn't make a mess and is a quick and easy step added to my PM routine now. I started with putting this around my nose, forehead and cheeks at night, where my large pores bother me the most, and then started using it on my whole face every night. My skin is sensitive and dry and not oily, so I didn't see a big difference with my pore, but this mask left my skin feeling very soft. My skin did not feel dried out at all, but I did follow it up with my moisturizer. I probably wouldn't have purchased this due to the price, but after trying it, I will order some once this is all used up and continue to use this as part of my PM routine.

[I received this product in exchange for my honest review] So this mask is a hit for me. It draws out all the impurity and leaves your skin feeling clean and pores less noticeable. It dries really fast but it doesn't pull tight like some clay mask. It's very comfortable but I will say if you have anything lurking under the surface like pimples or anything this mask will draw it out so you may notice a breakout afterwards but it goes away within a day
